name: Interior finish-out / TI (general)
summary: Tenant-improvement cost for a commercial shell is driven by use (retail soft goods < office < restaurant), MEP density, and first- vs. second-generation space (2nd gen runs 10-15% less per Cushman & Wakefield). Office fit-out is well benchmarked by Cushman & Wakefield's 2026 Americas Office Fit Out Cost Guide (US average $162/SF incl. a 10% contingency) with a published trade breakdown; retail and restaurant figures come from secondary sources (low confidence). Default = general commercial/office-grade TI.

typicalSize.method: Typical inline retail/restaurant 1,500-5,000 SF and office suites 3,000-25,000 SF; mid 6,000 SF is judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Mid = Cushman & Wakefield 2026 US average office fit-out $162/SF (e1) with its included 10% contingency removed (162 / 1.10 = $147) so the engine adds contingency separately; consistent with in-line retail ~$155/SF in 2025 (e4, secondary citation of C&W). City spread $108 (Cincinnati) - $219 (San Jose) (e2). Low = soft-goods retail low end $75/SF (e4) / 2nd-gen space (C&W: 10-15% discount, e1). High = full-service restaurant construction $250-400/SF (e4, e5).

scope.notes: Physical construction inside an existing shell (partitions, doors, ceilings, finishes, millwork, MEP/FP distribution, GC and fee), incl. OH&P. Excludes the base building/shell, low-voltage cabling, A/V, security, furniture/FF&E, signage permits and soft costs. C&W figures are 'limited to physical construction' (e3).

qualityTiers.method: Economy ~ low-cost market/2nd-gen soft goods (Cincinnati $108 x 0.85 2nd-gen / $147 = 0.62). Premium ~ San Jose $219 / $147 = 1.49 (rounded 1.45). Luxury ~ restaurant/high-end $350 / $147 = 2.4.

systemSplit.method: Cushman & Wakefield 2026 New York City hard-cost breakdown (e3) with the $20.41 contingency removed (base $200.21/SF): GR/GC & fee $21.84 -> 01 10.91%; millwork $13.12 -> 06 6.55%; doors/frames/hardware $21.45 -> 08 10.71%; drywall/acoustic/carpentry $26.29 + general finishes $13.63 -> 09 19.94%; misc. architectural trades $7.44 -> 10 3.72%; mechanical/plumbing/fire protection $50.19 (25.07%) split by judgment into 21 3.0%, 22 4.0%, 23 18.07%; electrical $46.25 -> 26 23.10%. For restaurants shift ~10 points from 09/06 to 22/23 (kitchen exhaust, grease, gas).

lineItems.name: Restaurant kitchen MEP premium (hood/exhaust & make-up air, grease waste, gas, walk-in, fire suppression)

cost.method: Restaurant construction $200-480/SF (QSR) and $250-400/SF (full service) (e4, e5) less the general TI mid $147/SF -> ~$75-250/SF premium; mid $150. Applied per SF of restaurant area.

lineItems.notes: Switch on for restaurant/food-service TI; kitchen equipment itself is FF&E.

cost.method: Estimating judgment; depends on whether the landlord provided one and on slab/site cutting. Verify locally.
Estimating judgment for aluminum storefront ~12 ft high incl. doors; usually landlord-provided in new shells.

lineItems.name: Low-voltage cabling, A/V and security (percent of hard cost)

cost.method: C&W tier ranges: IT 4-5% plus A/V 12-17% of hard cost (e1) = 16-22% x $147 = ~$24-32/SF; low for retail with minimal A/V, high for Tier-1 office.

perPrimaryUnit.method: C&W 2026 furniture ranges by market tier: Tier 3 $23.39-35.09, Tier 2 $27.54-41.32, Tier 1 $38.83-60.67 per SF (e1). Mid ~ Tier 2 high / Tier 1 low. Restaurant kitchen equipment and retail fixtures vary widely — override per concept.

pctOfHard.method: C&W soft costs as % of hard cost: Tier 1 10%, Tier 2 11%, Tier 3 13% (e1, e3).

softCosts.notes: Restaurants add licensing, health permits and kitchen design (judgment +2-4%).

design.method: Interior work in an existing shell; design contingency norm (judgment).

hard.method: C&W includes 'a ten percent (10%) contingency allowance' in its fit-out figures (e1; NYC example $20.41 of $220.62, e3). Raise toward 15% for 2nd-gen space with unknown existing conditions.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low 2nd-gen retail refresh ~ $60/SF; high = restaurant all-in ~ $535-555/SF incl. FF&E (e4) rounded up. Office all-in NYC $330.92 incl. furniture/IT/AV (e3) falls inside.

source.title: Americas Office Fit Out Cost Guide 2026

evidence.quote: broader U.S. average of $162 psf ... a ten percent (10%) contingency allowance has been included in the cost.
evidence.scopeNotes: Generation 1 corporate office fit-out, market conditions as of December 2025; excludes low-voltage, A/V, security, FF&E. Generation 2 (adaptive reuse of existing partitions/MEP) is 10-15% less. Tier tables give soft costs 10-13%, IT 4-5%, A/V 12-17%, furniture 20-24% of hard cost.

evidence.region: U.S. cities (Cincinnati low, San Jose high)

source.title: Office Fit Out Cost Guide (United States)

evidence.quote: San Jose at $219.32/psf (down from $219.47/psf) San Francisco at $219.26/psf ... New York City at $212.59/psf ... Indianapolis at $113.97/psf ... Kansas City at $108.26/psf ... Cincinnati at $108.03/psf
evidence.scopeNotes: Top-3 and bottom-3 US markets, 2026 guide, incl. 10% contingency.

source.title: Office Fit Out Cost Guide (United States)

evidence.quote: Mechanical, Plumbing, Fire Protection $50.19 Electrical $46.25 General Requirements, General Conditions and Fee $21.84 Contingency $20.41 TOTAL $220.62 ... Soft Costs: 10% $22.06 ... ALL-IN-TOTAL $330.92
evidence.scopeNotes: Full NYC breakdown also lists Misc. Architectural Trades $7.44, Millwork $13.12, Doors/Frames/Hardware $21.45, Drywall/Acoustic/Carpentry $26.29, General Finishes $13.63. Fit-out figures are 'limited to physical construction'.

source.title: Retail Build-Out Costs
source.publisher: GrowthFactor (blog, citing Cushman & Wakefield, Terrapin CG, KRG Hospitality)

evidence.quote: The national average for an in-line retail fit-out reached roughly $155 per square foot in 2025 ... Full-service ... $250–$400/SF construction ... All-in ~$555/SF on a 4,000 SF space
evidence.scopeNotes: Secondary aggregation; QSR $200-480/SF construction, ~$535/SF all-in with FF&E. Southeast ~$117/SF vs. Northern California ~$211/SF for the same store. Not verified against the primary C&W retail guide.

source.title: The Build-Out Process for Quick Service Restaurants

evidence.quote: The number you'll see cited most often is around $535 per square foot for a QSR build-out. ... A build in a second-tier market in a former restaurant space might come in at $200-250 per square foot.
evidence.scopeNotes: Contractor marketing guide, unsourced; $535 likely all-in incl. equipment. Manhattan first-time kitchen $800+.
